title: The Cost Of Protection
text:
The Cost Of Protection

August Gudmundsson, Cedric Gemehl

Gavekal Research | 14 Oct 2026

China appears to have accepted export restraints on hybrid cars in exchange for the European Union dialing down its confrontational trade rhetoric. The October 9 understanding gives EU leaders an opportunity to ease trade tensions as they gather for the European Council summit on October 15 and 16, where national leaders will discuss the broad direction of trade relations with China (see The EU Takes The Gloves Off).Under the deal, Beijing accepted a four-year cap on hybrid exports to the EU, starting in December 2026 at 350,000 vehicles—less than half the European Commission’s estimate of 800,000 for 2026—and rising 6% annually. Chinese brands’ share of the European hybrid market has jumped from 2% in 2024 to 16% in the first half of this year, making import restrictions a key EU demand.
